text:
Soojin Lee: Hey team — need updated Console screenshots for the marketplace refresh. Current ones are out of date (old nav + no onboarding wizard). Can we align today on WHICH pages we want to show?

Soojin Lee: AWS is asking for: 1 hero screenshot + 4–6 product screenshots. GCP wants fewer but prefers “setup + key workflow + monitoring”.

Soojin Lee: My draft list:
1) Marketplace onboarding wizard (org linking)
2) Entitlements status page (shows purchase → active)
3) Usage & cost analytics (token cost breakdown)
4) Model routing/rollout page (maybe too inside baseball?)
5) Audit logs / security settings (??)

Soojin Lee: What do we think? Also need confirmation on what’s safe to show (no customer data, no internal IDs).

Camila Reyes: +1 to wizard + usage analytics. That’s the “developer-first + enterprise-ready” story.

Camila Reyes: I’m less sure on audit logs page. If it’s behind an add-on / enterprise setting, we might get reviewer questions.

Ben Carter: For conversion: lead with “Get started in minutes” + “Understand spend”. So wizard + usage dashboard are must-haves.

Ben Carter: Anything about audit logs could be a separate diagram in the security packet rather than listing screenshots.

Elliot Price: Agree. Also if we screenshot audit logs/settings we have to be super careful about language consistency (esp. “retention” and “export”). If the UI says “coming soon” anywhere that’s a no-go.

Kira Thompson: From a docs POV, wizard screenshots are perfect because we can reuse them on the marketplace onboarding page (AWS + GCP) and keep everything consistent.

Kira Thompson: For the usage screenshot, can we show the “Tokens, latency, error rate” view vs cost? Or both?

Soojin Lee: Good q. We probably only get one “analytics” screenshot. What’s the strongest single view?

Chloe Martin: If we want one screenshot that reads clearly: “Usage → Cost” overview (time series + top models/routes + token cost). It’s the most visually legible.

Chloe Martin: Latency/error rate is more SRE-y and looks like any dashboard. The cost breakdown is more unique.

Ben Carter: +1 cost breakdown. Marketplace buyers are literally trying to route spend.

Camila Reyes: Another consideration: make sure the screenshot doesn’t imply pricing claims (“50% cheaper”) etc. Keep it neutral.

Soojin Lee: Ok so:
- Wizard (step view)
- Entitlements/status
- Usage & cost

Soojin Lee: Need 1–3 more. What about:
- Model catalog page (choose a model + “Redwood-verified performance profiles”)
- Dedicated capacity page (for enterprise)
- Private deployment (VPC) overview page (if we have a visual)

Connor O'Brien: If we show Dedicated/Private pages, make sure the UI is stable. Console changes are still landing this week.

Connor O'Brien: Also: marketplace reviewers sometimes reject screenshots that look “beta” / inconsistent.

Chloe Martin: Model catalog page is stable and looks clean.

Chloe Martin: Dedicated page exists but is somewhat empty if the org doesn’t have a cluster provisioned. We can stage a demo org with a “sample pool” but it’s a bit fake.

Elliot Price: I’d avoid “empty state” screenshots in listings.

Elliot Price: Model catalog is a safe 4th. It also supports Hosted SKU story.

Kira Thompson: If we do model catalog, can we capture one that shows “Streaming, tool calling, structured output” in a sidebar? That’s also consistent with listing copy.

Chloe Martin: Yes — there’s a “Capabilities” panel on the model details page. We can screenshot that.

Soojin Lee: Nice. That gives us:
1) Wizard
2) Entitlements status
3) Usage & cost
4) Model catalog/model detail

Soojin Lee: For the last slot: do we want a “rollouts / fallback policy” page? It’s a key differentiator.

Ben Carter: Rollouts might be too technical for the marketplace page, but it’s a good screenshot if it looks polished.

Camila Reyes: My worry: it invites questions like “is this included in base SKU?”

Elliot Price: Also rollout UI tends to contain internal model version strings that might confuse. If we do it, redact and use simple names.

Chloe Martin: We can stage it with friendly labels (e.g., “Llama-3.1-70B (pinned)”, “Fallback: Llama-3.1-8B”) and no UUIDs.

Soojin Lee: I’m leaning yes if we can keep it clean + not overpromise. Maybe label it as “Model management (version pinning + fallback)” in caption.

Camila Reyes: OK with that as long as captions are careful.

DESIGN BOT: Kira Thompson added a comment on “Marketplace Screenshot Inventory” (Figma) — section “Console pages to capture”.

Kira Thompson: I dropped the agreed list + notes here: https://figma.com/file/REDACTED-marketplace-screenshot-inventory (comment pinned)

Soojin Lee: Awesome. Next: who can actually produce/export these?

Chloe Martin: I can generate screenshots from staging (clean org). Need someone to confirm which region/account names are ok.

Elliot Price: Use “Redwood Demo Org” + “example@redwoodinference.com” and avoid showing AWS account IDs / org IDs. Also make sure no sidebar shows internal feature flags.

Connor O'Brien: Please coordinate w/ Release Eng for the build number — take screenshots after tomorrow’s Console deploy so nav matches the listing.

Ben Carter: Also please export in both 1280x720 and 1920x1080 if possible. GCP sometimes auto-crops.

Soojin Lee: Action items:
- Chloe: capture 5 screenshots (wizard, entitlements, usage & cost, model detail/capabilities, version pinning/fallback) post-deploy
- Elliot/Kira: quick review for redaction + wording consistency
- Soojin: update listing draft captions + send to AWS/GCP partner contacts

Camila Reyes: :thumbsup: Can we have first pass by EOD Thu?

Chloe Martin: Yep. I’ll post a folder link once exported.

Soojin Lee: Great — thanks all. (reactions: Camila Reyes :thumbsup: | Ben Carter :white_check_mark: | Elliot Price :eyes:)
